items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: I ran in and cut off the rehearsal... I went over the Vic’s drummer and I said, you may not know who I am but in around ten minutes I’m going to make my debut with the Count Basie orchestra, and I’m taking your cymbals and your sticks and your brushes, and incidentally what is your name please?

ctx.x: And if they didn’t tell you, you were doing okay. And he had a hard time firing people is that right?

Yes, most definitely. It’s very rare that you would be able to upset the Count. He was a very beautiful human being that had a lot of compassion and sensitivity for people. When he had to be total business he knew what to do. Unfortunately when he would receive information that one of the former members had maybe passed away or something like that, and we were in a rehearsal or just getting ready to go on stage or something, he would only give it two seconds thought, “Okay, straight ahead we have to go.” But…

Unfortunately my cymbals and my stick bag were left in New York City by accident. And fortunately enough, Vic Damone and a big orchestra, they were rehearsing to open up there the next day, in the little rehearsal room off to the side there. So I ran in and cut off the rehearsal and said, “Excuse me Bas’ I’ll be right with you,” and I went over the Vic’s drummer and I said, you may not know who I am but in around ten minutes I’m going to make my debut with the Count Basie orchestra, and I’m taking your cymbals…
